name: auth-layout
title: Auth layout
description: The sign-in split screen: a brand or narrative pane beside a centered credentials pane; one column on small screens.

when: Sign-in, sign-up and password reset pages.

builtIn: One main landmark; the brand pane is decoration on small screens.

AuthLayout.name: brandLogo
AuthLayout.description: Top of the brand pane — the logo lockup.

AuthLayout.name: brandContent
AuthLayout.description: Middle of the brand pane — kicker / headline / copy / stats.

AuthLayout.name: brandFooter
AuthLayout.description: Bottom of the brand pane — a low-key footer line.

AuthLayout.name: brandFooterLead
AuthLayout.description:
What rides at the start of the footer row, before `brandFooter` — a rule, a
mark, a motif. Nothing paints when it is absent: this layout carries no
signature of its own, so an app that wants one passes it.

AuthLayout.name: brandBackdrop
AuthLayout.description:
Decoration behind the brand pane's content. A slot rather than a choice —
the layout knows the geometry, the app knows what it wants to look like.

The pane is the positioning context and clips its overflow, so what goes
here should be `absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none` (and `aria-hidden`,
being decoration). It is rendered first and the pane's own rows carry
`relative`, so a backdrop that follows that shape sits behind them.

AuthLayout.name: brandClassName
AuthLayout.description:
The brand pane's own ground: its background and the text color its
contents inherit. The layout has no opinion, because the surface is where
two apps sharing this skeleton most need to differ.

AuthLayout.name: topRightSlot
AuthLayout.description: The credentials pane's corner control (top, inline end).

AuthLayout.name: credentialsElement
AuthLayout.description:
The credentials pane's element: `main` (default) when the layout is the page, `div` when the app's shell already
renders the page's one `<main>`.
